transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-04-28
- Start: 11:00 AM PDT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Brooks (Redwood Infra), Rajiv Kapoor (VeraHealth Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (VeraHealth Platform), Dr. Leah Kim (VeraHealth Product), Aaron Cho (VeraHealth SRE)

Auto-generated summary:
Redwood presented this week's benchmark run comparing Redwood serving runtime to VeraHealth's baseline vendor (BaselineVendorX). Redwood shows lower median and p95 latency and higher sustained throughput on the chat and completion workloads after tuning batching and enabling prefix KV cache. Customer raised questions about tail latency, cold-start behavior, and encryption/region residency for logs. Agreed next steps: share raw logs, run two additional workload profiles on baseline, and schedule a latency deep-dive with SREs.

Topics: Benchmark results, latency vs throughput tradeoffs, KV/prefix cache, batching configs, quantization impact, SLA targets, next steps for pilot scale-up

Action items (mentioned in call): see metadata field for owners and due dates

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll keep this tight\u00045 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Rajiv Kapoor: Rajiv here. Sofia, Leah, Aaron on our side.
[00:10] Sofia Martinez: Yep, Sofia.
[00:12] Ethan Patel: Ethan here from Redwood, thanks.
[00:15] Liam Brooks: Liam here, infra.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: run through the benchmark numbers we shipped, highlight tuning we did since last week, and align on what Vera runs on their baseline.

[00:30] Ethan Patel: Alright, so we ran three workloads, chat medium-length (avg 180 tokens), single-shot completions (avg 60 tokens), and batch embedding-ish throughput test. For the chat workload, Redwood p50 is ~110ms per request, p95 ~320ms, sustained throughput 220 req/s on the Dedicated pilot. BaselineVendorX numbers that Vera ran last week were p50 ~180ms, p95 ~680ms, throughput ~110 req/s on similar hardware.

[01:05] Rajiv Kapoor: Those p95 numbers look promising, can you clarify\u0011are you measuring end-to-end including network?

[01:12] Ethan Patel: Good question. We captured client-to-endpoint network RTT inside the same region, so numbers include e2e at the edge. We also exported raw traces so you can split network vs runtime. That's in the spreadsheet.

[02:05] Aaron Cho: Is KV cache enabled for the chat runs? Cold start behavior?

[02:12] Liam Brooks: Yes, prefix (KV) cache on by default for the chat scenario; cold start (first conversation) p95 does spike to ~750ms for long histories but after cache warmed it drops to the numbers I quoted. Cold-start is due to model weight page-in and warming the kv cache. We documented warmup steps.

[03:00] Dr. Leah Kim: For our SLA planning, we care a lot about 99th percentile for peak hours\u0011do you have 99 numbers?

[03:10] Ethan Patel: We do, and it's in the logs export. Roughly p99 for chat at our observed load was ~620ms steady-state, compared to BaselineVendorX's ~1.6s p99. There's more noise at p99, which is why we want to do a deep dive with Aaron.

[04:00] Rajiv Kapoor: What about quantization\u0011are you using 4-bit or 8-bit? We saw notes about mixed-precision in the doc.

[04:10] Liam Brooks: We're running two variants: a quantized int8 path for inference that keeps accuracy within 0.5% of float on our eval set, and a test int4 path which reduces latency ~15% but shows small regressions on longer contexts. For the public numbers today, it's the int8 quantized runtime.

[06:00] Sofia Martinez: Any backend differences\u0011like kernel selection or special attention kernels\u0011that cause the perf delta?

[06:12] Ethan Patel: Yes, kernel selection: our runtime auto-selects optimized kernels based on sequence length distribution. For the chat profile we hit an attention kernel optimized for mid-length sequences; BaselineVendorX appears to use a more generic path which increases per-token time. Also continuous batching in our serving layer helps during burst windows.

[08:30] Rajiv Kapoor: Can you explain continuous batching? We've seen batching hurt latency for some interactive workloads.

[08:40] Ethan Patel: Sure\u0011continuous batching batches small windows (we configure latency SLO caps) so request latency doesn't exceed your SLO; it uses small micro-batches to improve token throughput without large latency penalty. We tuned batch window to 8ms for your profile which gave the numbers I presented.

[11:20] Aaron Cho: About logs\u0011are logs and traces stored in our region and encrypted with customer-managed KMS? We need that for compliance.

[11:33] Maya Chen: Yes, for Private/Dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS and logs can be routed to your VPC. For hosted we centralize logs but we support encryption-at-rest with BYOK for premium plans. We'll attach the security doc.

[13:00] Rajiv Kapoor: Did you run a small model fallback test? Like if Dedicated queue is saturated, do we fall back to a cheaper variant?

[13:10] Ethan Patel: We did a fallback run\u0011requests redirected to a quantized 13B variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost; tech note: fallbacks retain KV cache compatibility if model architecture is variant-compatible. We included results in the spreadsheet\u0011fallback increased p95 by ~80ms.

[15:40] Dr. Leah Kim: On cost, the projected per-million token cost in your estimate looks 30% lower than BaselineVendorX but depends on batching assumptions. Can you share assumptions?

[15:52] Liam Brooks: Yes assumptions: average 140 tokens per request for chat accounting for prompts+responses, batching window 8ms, int8 quantization, 80% cache hit rate on repeat prefixes. We'll send the cost calc tab.

[18:00] Sofia Martinez: When you say 80% cache hit, what does that require from our side? Conversation IDs persisted?

[18:10] Ethan Patel: You need to surface a stable conversation key and we need sticky routing for that conversation to the same pool for a TTL\u0011storing keys in a Redis-like layer is optional. We can manage sticky routing on our side for Dedicated.

[20:00] Rajiv Kapoor: Any concerns with data residency? We need logs and model gradients (we don't send gradients) stored within EU for some customers.

[20:12] Maya Chen: For Private and Dedicated we can pin region and ensure logs stay within EU. We'll include a region pinning note in the security doc.

[22:00] Ethan Patel: Quick note on methodology: both Redwood and Vera's baseline runs used the same load generator but there were two small diffs\u0011baseline used slightly older kernel drivers (we emulated similar hardware) and they had a higher context-window average which we standardized post-hoc. We flagged that in the spreadsheet.

[25:00] Aaron Cho: Can you re-run the chat test but with 6ms batch window? I suspect that'll reduce p95 further, but might hit throughput.

[25:10] Ethan Patel: We can, we'll run 6ms and 10ms runs and share the delta. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and ops/s.

[28:00] Rajiv Kapoor: For the additional workloads Vera will run\u0011what exactly do you need from us?

[28:05] Maya Chen: Two things: 1) run a chat profile (180 tokens avg) and 2) a short completion profile (60 tokens) on your baseline vendor with the same client-to-endpoint setup and provide raw logs & the load generator config. We'll compare apples-to-apples.

[30:00] Dr. Leah Kim: On the pilot timeline, if these numbers keep holding, we'd like to expand to a 2-week production shadow in mid-May. That ok?

[30:10] Maya Chen: That sounds reasonable. We'll confirm capacity for your expected qps and propose Dedicated pilot terms in an email.

[33:00] Sofia Martinez: Any gotchas about autoscaling? We had problems where scale-up was slow under short spikes previously.

[33:12] Liam Brooks: Our Dedicated autoscaler supports proactive warm pools and burst capacity. For short spikes we recommend keeping a small warm pool and enabling burst capacity; we'll show config examples.

[35:00] Rajiv Kapoor: Competitors also pitch multi-region fallback\u0011how do you compare?

[35:10] Maya Chen: We support multi-region routing with automated fallback and region-aware KV cache; the tricky bit is cache priming across regions but we have policies to avoid cold-start storms.

[37:00] Aaron Cho: Ok last technical\u0011what instrumentation are you including in the logs? I want per-token timings and kernel-level breakdown.

[37:12] Ethan Patel: We emit per-token latency buckets, kernel selection, batch size, and cache hit metadata. That's in the raw traces.

[40:00] Maya Chen: Recap\u0011Ethan runs two extra batch-window tests (6ms, 10ms) and posts results + raw logs by Friday 2026-04-30. Vera runs two workloads on baseline and uploads logs by 2026-05-05. Schedule a deep dive for 2026-05-06 with Aaron and Ethan. Maya to send updated Dedicated pilot pricing and capacity note by 2026-05-01.

[41:00] Rajiv Kapoor: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[41:05] Dr. Leah Kim: Thanks, bye.
[41:10] Sofia Martinez: Bye.
[41:12] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

End of meeting.
